slides.title: Confession: I kept a gift I hated for 6 years because of guilt
slides.sub: Here's how I let go now

slides.title: The gift did its job the day you opened it. You don't owe it a shelf forever.
Ask: do I use it or love it?
slides.body: If neither, it's a 'thank you' that already happened. It's allowed to leave.

slides.title: Give it a 30-day box
slides.body: New gifts you're unsure about go in one box with a date on it. Unused by then? Donate, no re-deciding.

slides.title: Thank the person, not the thing
slides.body: Send the thank-you text, then let the object go. The kindness stays with you.

slides.title: Make a wish list early
slides.body: Share a short list of things you'd use. Fewer guilt gifts land in the first place.

slides.title: Get the declutter pages
slides.body: The Tidy Brain Printable Pack has a declutter tracker and the 5-bin decision flow. Link in bio.

caption:
Gift guilt is so real in December.
What's the gift you've been keeping out of guilt?
